headline: Friday's 29,000 US payrolls print pushed an October Fed hike out of the price and has lifted Asia on Monday, with the Nikkei up 2.34 percent and Taiwan up 2.24 percent, as India reopens from a holiday into a Reserve Bank decision on Wednesday after an eighth straight weekly Nifty loss.

summary.us: The S and P 500 closed Friday at 7,722.72, up 0.73 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent to 27,190.86 after September nonfarm payrolls came in at 29,000 against roughly 84,000 expected and unemployment rose to 4.2 percent, which cut October Fed hike pricing and sent the VIX down 6.59 percent to 15.31. Tesla gained 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries, about 5.3 percent above a company compiled consensus of 461,974, and Nvidia rose 1.34 percent to an intraday record after its board added 150 billion dollars to the buyback authorization, while the 10 year Treasury yield still ended at 5.277 percent, up 1.79 percent over the week.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed Thursday at 22,421.95, down 0.88 percent, and the Bank Nifty slipped 0.33 percent to 54,450.75, with Friday a Gandhi Jayanti holiday, leaving the index on an eighth straight weekly decline as foreign investors sold a net 9,484.20 crore rupees in the cash segment against domestic institutional buying of 10,041.80 crore rupees. India VIX jumped 7.19 percent to 14.46, Bajaj Auto fell 7.62 percent after September sales of 538,443 units with domestic volumes down 9 percent, PB Fintech dropped 7.89 percent to its 980 rupee issue price on the IRDAI commission consultation paper, and the rupee sat at 96.30 to the dollar.
summary.global: Hong Kong was the weak spot on Friday, with the Hang Seng down 2.60 percent to 23,972.29, its steepest fall in more than six months, as high US yields and the suspension of Stock Connect southbound trading until October 8 removed mainland buying, while Europe closed higher with the DAX up 1.17 percent and the FTSE 100 up 0.32 percent. Monday's Asian session has the Nikkei at 69,907.85, up 2.34 percent, and Taiwan up 2.24 percent, Brazil's Ibovespa rose 2.63 percent to 192,115 on the eve of Sunday's general election, and gold at 4,183.10 dollars an ounce is still down 3.2 percent over the week.

Delta Air Lines third quarter results and the University of Michigan preliminary October consumer sentiment reading

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.
